Federal Register /  Vol. 46, No. 12 /  M onday, January 19,1981 /  Presidential Documents 4675
Presidential Documents
Executive Order 12270 of January 15, 1981
President’s Council on Spinel Cord Injury
By the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution of the United 
States of Am erica, and in order to establish, in accord with the Federal 
Advisory Committee Act, as amended (5 U.S.C. App. I), an advisory commit­
tee on spinal cord injury, it is hereby ordered as follow s;
established a President s Council on Spinal Cord Injury which 
shall be composed of twelve members appointed by the President.
1-102. The Committee shall advise the President, through the Secretary of 
Education, on appropriate responses to the goals of prevention, diagnosis, 
treatment, and reversal of spinal cord injury.
1-103. The Secretary of Education shall provide the Council with such admin­
istrative services and support as may be necessary.
1-104. Notwithstanding the provisions of any other Executive Order, the 
functions of the President under the Federal Advisory Committee A ct (5 U.S.C. 
App. I), except that of reporting annually to the Congress, w hich are applica­
ble to the Council, shall be performed by the Secretary of Education in 
accordance with guidelines and procedures established by the Adm inistrator 
of G eneral Services.
1-105. The Committee shall term inate on D ecem ber 31, 1981, unless sooner 
extended.
THE W H ITE HOUSE, 
Ja n u a r y  15, 1981.
[FR Doc. 81-2045 
Filed 1-15-81; 3:30 pm] 
Billing code 3195-01-M

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: whole: Establishment of the President's Council on Spinal Cord Injury (twelve members appointed by the President) under the Federal Advisory Committee Act to advise the President through the Secretary of Education (secs. 1-101, 1-102), Education Department support (sec. 1-103), FACA functions to the Secretary of Education except the annual report to Congress (sec. 1-104), and termination on December 31, 1981 (sec. 1-105). Ended with the whole order: first end EO 12270, 1981-12-31. The order's own sec. 1-105 fixes the termination on December 31, 1981; that is a termination date, not a report deadline (the only reporting wording, in sec. 1-104, reserves the FACA annual report to Congress to the President and sets no end). 'Unless sooner extended' is a condition no held instrument met. Later event attached: EO 12553 revocation (1986-02-25), which does not move the first end.

later_events.mechanism: formal revocation after the end: express revocation by EO 12553 ('it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and any amendments thereto, are revoked:', followed by the table row 12270 'Establishing the President's Council on Spinal Cord Injury'); EO 12553 has no effective-date wording, so the revocation took effect on signing, February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, printed March 3, 1986; filed February 26, 1986); the Council had already terminated on 1981-12-31, so this clears a spent order and does not move the first end

research_rationale: EO 12270 (signed 1981-01-15, 46 FR 4675), read in full from the held official FR text: enacting words and secs. 1-101 to 1-105 establishing the President's Council on Spinal Cord Injury with its own termination date. The dossier's single clause (#whole, 'By the authority vested' through 'unless sooner extended.') is the whole operative text; the OCR layer drops the opening words of sec. 1-101 ('1-101. There is') and prints 'Spinel' in the heading, PDF-check items that do not change the clause boundary or sec. 1-105. Inventory confirmed without correction. EO 12553 (signed 1986-02-25, effective on signing; the record ACT:EO:12270>EO:12553 is an agent-located Rastell record upheld by an independent AI reviewer with a D6 step; simulated ingestion, not yet in the committed build) revokes it by number. D6 / earlier-end test (did any instrument other than EO 12553, or the order's own dated term, end the order or a clause before 1986-02-25?): The order's own sec. 1-105 fixes the termination on December 31, 1981; that is a termination date, not a report deadline (the only reporting wording, in sec. 1-104, reserves the FACA annual report to Congress to the President and sets no end). 'Unless sooner extended' is a condition no held instrument met. The by-number scan finds 12270 only in EO 12553 (the EO 9630 hit is an FR page number); 'Spinal Cord Injury' appears in no other held order text; the OFR catalog records only the EO 12553 revocation. EO 12258 (1980-12-31, continuing advisory committees) predates the order and does not list it; the later continuance and termination orders EO 12305 and EO 12399 do not name it or the Council. EO 12270's end rests on its own words, not on a whole-text restatement or on an event that does not name it, so the open owner method question raised in the probe does not arise here. EO 12553 (1986-02-25) is therefore only an upper bound: the first end is the 1981-12-31 sunset, and EO 12553 is attached as a later event. Same pattern as the probe's EO 12269 (the companion small-business committee order signed the same day). The end source is the held official FR text, not the American Presidency Project transcription that the dossier's own-term leads also cite, so nothing relies on the pending transcription-as-copy ruling, nor on the report-deadline ruling. First end: EO 12270, 1981-12-31. Savings: none_after_bounded_search (see savings_residuals). AI producer hypothesis only; not human certification and not a status.
